cities.base: lakeside village, alternative Tatra base and the trailhead for Popradské pleso

places.name: Popradské pleso
places.note: Out and back from Strbske Pleso, about 5.5km each way and under 200m of gain, 3.5 to 4 hours; well marked, no guide needed, past the Symbolic Cemetery. Busy by midday in July and August.

places.name: Lomnický štít cable car
places.note: Two-stage lift to 2,634 m; book the exact slot, capacity is small and summit time is about 30 to 50 minutes. Out of service 16 to 27 Nov 2026, running 28 and 29 Nov and 5 and 6 Dec, fully back from 12 Dec; often cancelled for wind, fares not confirmed, check vt.sk.

places.name: Main Square (Hlavné námestie)
places.note: Small, compact old town, easy to walk in an hour or two. Old Town Hall and the Napoleon soldier statue are here, pleasant rather than dazzling.

places.name: Bratislava Castle
places.note: Rebuilt boxy exterior, but the terrace view over the Danube is the reason to come up. EUR 14 covers interior, Treasury and Northern Walls, 22 with the Museum of History; 10:00 to 18:00, last entry 17:00, closed Tuesday. Grounds 08:00 to 22:00, baroque garden 09:00 to 16:00 in winter.

places.name: UFO Observation Deck, SNP Bridge
places.note: Sunset slot is worth it. Skip the separate observation ticket and just eat at the restaurant up there instead, same view, no entry fee if you're dining.

places.name: St. Martin's Cathedral
places.note: Coronation church of the Kingdom of Hungary for centuries, plain inside for that history. Entry reported free, the crypt by tour; Mon to Sat 08:00 to 20:00, Sundays only 13:45 to 16:30 per a listing, not the church. A 45 minute stop.

places.name: Slavín War Memorial
places.note: Burial ground and memorial for about 7,000 Soviet soldiers on a hill above the diplomatic quarter, with good city views. Quiet, most tourists never make it up; a 20 minute uphill walk, open-air with no set hours.

places.name: Štrbské Pleso lake and village
places.note: A glacial lake at 1,346 m, up to 20 m deep and iced over about 155 days a year, with a well-kept shore path and Hotel Patria as the landmark. Easy and flat, good for an arrival evening and again before dinner; crowded with day-trippers at midday in summer.

places.name: Devín Castle
places.note: Ruins on a bluff over the Danube and Morava confluence, Austria across the water; the view is the draw. Winter 10:00 to 16:00, last entry 45 min before, closed Mondays, EUR 6. A winter page says Tue to Fri only and the upper castle shut, so check.

places.name: Danube-Morava Confluence Viewpoint
places.note: Free lookout below the castle walls where the two rivers visibly meet in different colors. Worth the short walk down even if you skip paying for the castle interior.

places.name: Devín Village Riverside Walk
places.note: Small quiet village beneath the castle, a few houses and a riverside path. Nothing to plan around but pleasant while waiting for a bus back to the city.

places.name: Bus 29 from Bratislava (Nový Most / Most SNP)
places.note: The actual way most visitors get to Devín, roughly 20-25 minutes from the city center. Buy a ticket before boarding, it is checked.

places.name: Kaviareň Devín (castle-view café)
places.note: Simple riverside café near the castle entrance for a coffee or ice cream before heading back. Nothing special about the food, the setting carries it.

places.name: Devín Amphitheatre ruins
places.note: Minor foundation remnants within the castle grounds, easy to miss and not worth seeking out separately from the main ruins walk.

places.name: Devín Castle Small Exhibition (Well Tower)
places.note: Small exhibit on the site from Great Moravia to the Habsburgs, covered by the EUR 6 castle ticket counted on the castle row, so check the price there. Winter 10:00 to 16:00, closed Mondays; skippable, the view matters more.

places.name: Devín Riverside Lawn
places.note: Open grass area by the water below the castle, good for a packed lunch on a warm afternoon before the bus back. Bring your own food, there is little around it.

places.name: Freedom Bridge (Most Slobody) to Austria
places.note: Pedestrian/cycle bridge over the Morava into Austria, built after the Iron Curtain fell. Symbolically interesting but adds an hour round trip for a view no better than the confluence lookout already gives you.

places.name: Devín Castle Entrance Kiosk
places.note: Small souvenir and ticket stand at the entrance, standard postcards and replica coins, nothing distinctive.

places.name: Last Bus 29 back to Bratislava
places.note: Service thins out in the evening and stops earlier than the castle's closing time in shoulder season. Check the timetable before you commit to a late visit, there is no taxi rank waiting here.

places.name: Starý Smokovec village and promenade
places.note: Small strip of old wooden hotel buildings and a train station, more a base than a destination. Fine for an arrival evening stroll, nothing to build a day around.

places.name: Hrebienok Funicular (Starý Smokovec station)
places.note: The only funicular in Slovakia, 1,937 m long from 1,025 m up to 1,272 m in about 7 minutes, and it saves an hour of uphill walking. Back in service from 5 Nov 2026 to 18 Apr 2027 after autumn maintenance; fares and timetable not rechecked, see vt.sk, and buy the return.

places.name: Studenovodské vodopády (Cold Stream Waterfalls)
places.note: Well-marked cascades on the Studeny potok at about 1,230 m, a short walk past Hrebienok and part of the loop to Zamkovskeho chata rather than a separate trip, 4.9 from 472 Komoot hikers. Pretty without being dramatic.

places.name: Zamkovského chata
places.note: Historic mountain hut, no road access, everything carried up; 4.7 on Google from 3,052. Goulash, halusky and pirohy, the lunch stop on the Hrebienok loop. Menu prices are not published, so treat the cost as a guide.

places.name: Route: Hrebienok to Zamkovského chata loop via waterfalls
places.note: Funicular to Hrebienok (1198m), past the Studenovodske waterfalls to Zamkovskeho chata (1475m), loop back down: 5 to 6 hours door to door, moderate and well signed. The map point is the funicular station where it starts.

places.name: Route: Tatranská Lomnica to Skalnaté pleso short walk (wind-day fallback)
places.note: Low-elevation forest walk from Tatranská Lomnica towards the lower cable car station, usable when wind shuts the high ground and Lomnický štít is cancelled. About 2-2.5 hrs round trip, minimal elevation gain, no exposure to weather closures.

places.name: Tatranská galéria (Poprad, satellite exhibit in Tatranská Lomnica)
places.note: Small regional gallery, closed Mondays. Only worth it as a rain-day filler, not a reason to detour on a clear day.

places.name: St Egidius Square, Poprad
places.note: Poprad's long main square, 4.7 from 33 Komoot cyclists, and quickly done on its own; the better half is Spisska Sobota under 2 km away, with its 1516 Master Paul altar. Free and open-air, an easy add-on to a train change in Poprad.

places.name: Skalnaté pleso
places.note: Small tarn at the midstation of the Lomnicky stit cable car, worth the short stop while waiting for the connecting lift. The cable car is out of service 16 to 27 Nov and again 30 Nov to 4 Dec 2026, so on those days it is a long walk up.

places.name: Chata pri Zelenom plese
places.note: Longer, quieter hike from Tatranská Lomnica up to the Green Lake chata, roughly 5 hours round trip. Fewer crowds than the Hrebienok side. Good option if you've already done the standard routes and want a second real hiking day.

places.name: Furkotská dolina lower valley walk
places.note: Flat forest track on the valley floor below the ridge, no exposure, open when wind closes the passes; roughly 2 hours out and back, or the full Furkotska loop, 12.6 km and about 4 hours. The Strbske Pleso lifts are listed shut until 5 Dec 2026, so walk up and down.

places.name: Koliba Kamzík
places.note: Wooden koliba-style restaurant doing Slovak standards, halušky and grilled meats. Sits right in the village so it's the easy dinner after a hiking day, nothing exceptional but reliable and warm.

places.name: Hotel Patria restaurant
places.note: Sits right on the lakeshore, the dining room has the view the village is named for. Food is fine hotel fare, you're paying for the setting at sunset more than the cooking.

places.name: View of the Ski Jump at Štrbské Pleso
places.note: Viewpoint on the jump towers built for the 1970 Nordic World Ski Championships, 4.8 from 191 Komoot visitors, with a wooden chamois sculpture beside it. Nothing to do at the towers themselves; a 20 minute look on the walk round the lake.

places.name: Tatranská Lomnica village
places.note: Skip unless you're using it as the trailhead for Zelené pleso. The village itself is scattered spa-era buildings and a small zoo, nothing that justifies a special trip on a three-night stay already full of better hikes.

places.name: Slovak Pub
places.note: Slovak pub on Obchodná with bryndzove halusky on the menu. Set lunch EUR 9.50 (listing checked Nov 2026), dinner costs more; weekdays from 11:00, weekends from 12:00, to 22:00.

places.name: Zylinder Cafe and Restaurant
places.note: Cafe-restaurant on Hviezdoslav Square: bryndzove halusky EUR 12, Hungarian goulash 17, Pressburg schnitzel 16, pikeperch 19.50 on its own (undated) menu. Mon to Sat to 23:00, Sundays to 22:00.

places.name: Modrá Hviezda
places.note: Slovak restaurant below the castle: duck EUR 24.90, game goulash 22.50, mains 19.90 to 31.90 (own menu, 2026). Weekdays 17:30 to 22:00, weekends from 12:00; one listing says closed Mondays and it shuts 18 Nov, so hours vary, check.

places.name: Old Town Hall
places.note: City museum in the Old Town Hall on the Main Square, Tue to Sun 10:00 to 18:00, closed Mondays (winter 2025/26 hours). The ticket price was not found, so check the price; the map point is the courtyard.

places.name: Primate's Palace
places.note: Built 1781 for Archbishop Batthyány; six English tapestries of the 1630s were found hidden in its walls, and the Hall of Mirrors is the room to see. EUR 5, 2.50 over 60. For 16 to 22 Nov 2026 the city lists it open only Tue and Sun 10:00 to 17:00, so check the week.

places.name: Slovak National Gallery
places.note: National art collection in the neo-Renaissance Esterházy Palace, refurbished 2017. About USD 7 adult; 10:00 to 18:00 Tue, Wed and Fri to Sun, Thursday 12:00 to 20:00, closed Mondays.

places.name: Grassalkovich Palace (Presidential Palace)
places.note: Built 1760 as the summer residence of the head of the Hungarian Royal Chamber, the presidential seat since 1996. The interior is shut; the garden behind it is free, daily 08:00 to 21:00, a 30 minute stroll.

places.name: Michael's Gate
places.note: The last surviving gate of the medieval walls, from about 1300, a 51 m tower with the city weapons exhibition inside. Free to see from the street; tower ticket not found, so check the price. Winter 10:00 to 18:00, closed Tuesdays.

places.name: Blue Church (Church of St Elizabeth)
places.note: Art Nouveau church of the early 1900s, 4.6 on Google from 13,083; the exterior is the point. Free, but the door is only open around Mass times, so hours vary, check.
places.neighborhood: East edge of the Old Town

places.name: Slowenská reštaurácia
places.note: Falstaff 2026 gives it 88 points: trout EUR 19.10, duck 18.70, venison 17.90, mains 16.50 to 25.90 (July 2026 menu). Daily 11:30 to 22:00, kitchen to 21:30.

places.name: Starý Šmakovec
places.note: 4.7 on Google from 3,270: bryndza halusky EUR 14.40, trout 16.90, goulash 18.90 (undated own menu). Winter Fri to Sun only, 11:00 to 22:00, kitchen to 21:00; closed 16 to 19 Nov 2026.

places.name: Museum of the Tatra National Park (TANAP)
places.note: Continues the Carpathian Museum begun in Poprad in 1883 and was set up by the park in 1957: botany, zoology, geology, maps and folk life, with a 3.2 ha garden of about 270 species in summer. Winter 08:30 to 12:00 and 13:00 to 16:00, reopened 18 Nov; check the price.

places.name: Bilíkova chata
places.note: Mountain hut on the way up from Starý Smokovec towards Hrebienok. Opening hours and prices not found, so hours vary, check before counting on a meal there.

places.name: Koliba Patria
places.note: The Hotel Patria koliba: beef goulash EUR 18.50, trout 21.90, pork tenderloin 17.50, mains 13.50 to 27.90 (2026 menu). Daily 11:30 to 21:00, one listing says to 22:30 Fri and Sat; book ahead.

places.name: Reštaurácia Furkotka
places.note: Traditional Slovak with outdoor seating, 4.6 on Google from 2,029. About USD 20 to 30 a head from an undated listing, so check; daily 11:00 to 23:00.

places.name: Skok waterfall (Mlynická dolina)
places.note: A 25 m fall on the Mlynica stream at 1,720 m, 5.0 from 251 Komoot hikers, a half-day hike up Mlynicka dolina from the village. The trail to the fall is open all year but the route above it is shut from November to early June; snow in winter, so check conditions.

places.name: Symbolic Cemetery (Symbolický cintorín)
places.note: Over 160 plaques and about 50 carved, painted wooden crosses for those killed in the Tatras, begun in 1936 by the painter Otakar Stafl and opened 1940, under the walls of Ostrva. Free, a few minutes past the hotel at Popradske pleso; closed 15 Dec to 31 May, open now.

places.name: Starý Smokovec station, Tatra Electric Railway
places.note: The station that made the resort: it opened on 17 Dec 1908 with the first stage of the metre-gauge line from Poprad and became the junction when the Strbske Pleso line was finished in 1912. Look at the three-storey half-timbered building; free to see, fares not checked.

places.name: Hrebienok bear sculptures
places.note: Iron and wooden bears at the top of the funicular, 4.7 from 165 Komoot visitors, with snack stalls and views to Slavkovsky stit and Lomnicky stit. Free and twenty minutes; the funicular runs again from 5 Nov 2026. Real bears live here too, so keep to the park rules.

places.name: Rainerova chata (Rainer Hut)
places.note: Built in 1865 for visitors to the Cold Water Falls, the oldest preserved shelter on the south side of the High Tatras, no longer a working hut. In June 2024 the red trail from Hrebienok was shut for rockfall, with a detour on the green trail past Bilikova chata; check tatry.sk first.

places.name: Kežmarok Castle museum
places.note: First recorded in 1463 and the only fully preserved castle in Spis, 4.6 from 4,767 Google reviews; guided tours only, through the Thokoly rooms, chapel, guilds and arms. Winter hours are not published and the adult fare was not found, so check the price; old cars 3 EUR extra.

places.name: Articular Wooden Church, Kežmarok
places.note: A 17th century UNESCO wooden church built without nails, seating 1,500 under a blue painted ceiling, 4.8 on Google. Guided entry about every half hour, 3 to 5 EUR with the New Evangelical Church; from 09:00 weekdays, 09:30 Sat, shut at noon and Sunday, check winter.

places.name: Spišská Sobota historic centre
places.note: First recorded in 1256 and a monument reserve since 1950: St George's church, Gothic from 1464, holds a 1516 altar from Master Paul of Levoca's workshop, beside a 1598 Renaissance bell tower. The square is free; church hours and price not found, so check.

places.name: Spiš Castle
places.note: One of the largest castle complexes in Central Europe, 41,426 m2 inside its walls on a 634 m travertine hill. Closed from 18 Nov 2026 and December to March, so not this month; 8 EUR adult, 09:00 to 17:00 in October, to 19:00 May to September.

outings.why: A moderate, well-marked lake walk through the Symbolický cintorín war memorial, no guide needed but it's a real 3.5-4 hr hike, not a stroll.
outings.name: Popradské pleso out-and-back
outings.season: June to September, snow possible on peaks even in June

outings.why: Funicular up to Hrebienok, loop past the waterfalls to the chata for lunch and back down; the standard Tatra day but still 5-6 hrs door to door.
outings.name: Hrebienok to Zamkovského chata via Studenovodské vodopády
outings.fallback: Skip the waterfall loop and just ride the funicular up for the view if the weather turns.

outings.why: The high-altitude alternative to the waterfall loop on a clear day, but it's frequently wind-cancelled so don't count on it as your only mountain day.
outings.name: Lomnický štít cable car
outings.fallback: Do the Hrebienok waterfall loop instead.

outings.why: A 20-minute bus out to ruins on a river bluff, worth it for the view over the Danube/Morava confluence more than the ruins themselves.
outings.name: Devín Castle half day
outings.season: Closed or limited Nov-March, confirm in shoulder season

destination.name: Slovakia: Bratislava + High Tatras
destination.pitch: A small capital bookending three days of proper mountain walking in the High Tatras — don't stretch it thinner by chasing Košice or the east.
destination.caveat: The whole trip's activity hinges on Tatra weather; two rainy days up there and you're stuck in a mountain village with no backup nearby. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Bratislava Old Town and the UFO deck give you one pleasant, low-effort city day on each end.
because.nature: Popradské pleso and the Hrebienok waterfall loop are real Tatra hiking, not scenic-overlook tourism.
because.culture: Bratislava and Devín Castles cover a half-day each of low-stakes history.
because.adventure: Lomnický štít cable car and the Symbolický cintorín ridge walk are the closest this trip gets to adrenaline, weather permitting.
